entries.sense_en: shabby and run-down, looking poor and not respectable

synonyms.nuance: Worn and old-looking; says nothing about morals.
Untidy and unkempt, more casual and often about people.
Seedy plus a hint of dishonesty or vice; stronger disapproval.

entries.sense_en: looking so bad that nobody would respect it

synonyms.nuance: Suggests dishonest dealings, used for people and businesses.
Rare and plain; disreputable is the usual word.
Widely known for something bad; about fame, not appearance.

entries.sense_en: damaged or in poor condition from long use

synonyms.nuance: Completely used up; the worse for wear can still be usable.
Damaged by knocks and hard treatment, not just age.
Informal American word for something in rough shape.

entries.tip_ko: 사람에게 쓰면 '지치고 초라해 보이는'이라는 뜻도 된다.

entries.sense_en: completely without something (used with 'of')

synonyms.nuance: Missing something needed; less absolute than devoid.
Plain and concrete; devoid of is more formal and abstract.
Usually positive: without something unwanted.

entries.tip_ko: devoid of + 명사 형태로 외워 두자.

entries.sense_en: strange and unusual in a curious, amusing way

synonyms.nuance: Pleasantly odd and unconventional; common in modern speech.
Changing suddenly and unpredictably; often negative.
Coming from imagination rather than reality.

entries.sense_en: to mention something indirectly (used with 'to')

synonyms.nuance: Mention directly by name; allude only hints.
Suggest something without saying it, often to make someone guess.
synonyms.example: He hinted that he might quit.

synonyms.nuance: Say something briefly and openly.

entries.sense_en: an old word for a round, hard felt hat like a bowler

synonyms.nuance: The normal name today for a round, hard felt hat.
synonyms.example: a man in a bowler hat

synonyms.nuance: American word for the same hat.

entries.sense_en: a cheerful, noisy celebration, often with drinking

synonyms.nuance: Slightly old-fashioned; cheerful festivity in general.
Neutral, any marking of a special event.
Wild, loud partying, more intense.

entries.sense_en: a person who attacks someone violently

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; assailant is formal, used in news and law.
Attacks in the street specifically to rob.
The one who starts a fight or war.

entries.sense_en: to run away quickly, usually out of fear

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, plain description of running away.
Formal; escaping from real danger.
Dash away suddenly, like a startled animal.

entries.sense_en: a confusing network of paths or streets where it is easy to get lost

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word, also for puzzles and games; labyrinth is more literary.
A crowded tangle of narrow passages or rooms.
Neutral; does not suggest getting lost.

entries.sense_en: so perfect that it cannot be doubted or criticized
entries.sense_ko: 나무랄 데 없는, 의심할 여지가 없는

synonyms.nuance: Faultless in quality or manners.
Formal; behavior that cannot be blamed.
No defects at all; about things more than character.

entries.tip_ko: 여기서는 유머러스한 과장: 흠잡을 데 없는 거위.

entries.sense_en: looking inward, thinking deeply about one's own thoughts

synonyms.nuance: Thoughtful, not necessarily about oneself.
Calm, quiet, deep thought.
A personality type (shy), not an act of thinking.

entries.sense_en: a move backward to a worse state

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for gradual worsening.
Going back to an earlier, often childish or less developed state.
Getting steadily worse in condition or quality.

entries.sense_en: to have become poor or unlucky after a better time

synonyms.nuance: The usual modern phrase for losing money and comfort.
synonyms.example: The family fell on hard times.

synonyms.nuance: Losing social position or wealth.
synonyms.example: He has come down in the world.

entries.modern: "fallen upon evil days" → "fallen on hard times"

entries.sense_en: spending much time sitting, with little exercise

synonyms.nuance: General: not doing much of anything.
Tied to a desk by one's work.
Not moving at all right now; describes an object, not a lifestyle.

entries.tip_ko: 라틴어 sedere(앉다)에서 온 말: a sedentary job(앉아서 하는 일).

entries.sense_en: streaked or mixed with grey (of hair or beard)

synonyms.nuance: Plain description; fully grey.
Pretty, positive, shining grey or white.
Informal: dark hair mixed evenly with grey.

entries.sense_en: to rub with oil or cream (here, hair cream)

synonyms.nuance: Simple word; anoint sounds old and formal, or religious.
Spread messily or thickly.
Everyday verb for putting oil on something.

entries.tip_ko: 종교 의식에서 '기름 부음'을 뜻하는 단어이기도 하다.

entries.sense_en: a protest or complaint, often a mild scolding

synonyms.nuance: Common word; may be public and strong.
A stated disagreement with something.
Blames or shows disappointment, more personal.

entries.sense_en: to lose money or social standing

synonyms.nuance: Same meaning, equally common.
synonyms.example: He has come down in the world.

synonyms.nuance: Focuses on money trouble.
synonyms.example: a family that fell on hard times

entries.tip_ko: 반대말은 go up in the world / rise in the world.

entries.sense_en: seeming reasonable and likely to be true

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; easy to believe.
Deserving to be trusted, about sources and evidence.
Actually persuades you; plausible only seems possible.

entries.sense_en: hard animal fat used to make candles

synonyms.nuance: Candles today are usually wax; tallow is animal fat and smells.
Any oily fat; less specific.
Hard fat from around beef or mutton kidneys, used in cooking.

entries.sense_en: burning weakly and flickering, about to go out (of a candle)

synonyms.nuance: Shaking light; does not say the flame is dying.
Plainly about to go out.
With small popping noises as it burns badly.

entries.tip_ko: 녹은 촛농이 홈(gutter)을 이루며 흘러내리는 모습에서 온 말.

entries.sense_en: sparkling brightly with quick flashes of light

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for small bright flashes.
Bright, often gold or showy.
So bright it almost hurts the eyes.

entries.tip_ko: sc는 [s]로 읽고 강세는 첫 음절: SIN-tuh-lay-ting.

entries.sense_en: valuable things found hidden or by chance

synonyms.nuance: A hidden stash someone has saved up.
Any lucky discovery.
Sudden lucky money, not a physical object.

entries.tip_ko: 'treasure trove'는 지금은 '값진 것이 가득한 곳'이라는 비유로도 쓴다.

entries.sense_en: to guess from incomplete evidence

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; may have no evidence at all.
synonyms.example: I guess it cost a lot.

synonyms.nuance: Think about possibilities with little proof, often at length.
Formal; a guess from a few clues.

entries.modern: "can only be conjectured" → "can only be guessed"

entries.sense_en: to drop or sit down heavily and suddenly

synonyms.nuance: Fall down loosely, tired or careless.
Fall because of weakness or exhaustion.
Informal: put or sit down heavily.

entries.sense_en: to take something away secretly, to steal (formal, legal)

synonyms.nuance: Plain and direct.
Steal small things little by little.
Neutral; does not say it is a crime.

entries.tip_ko: '추상적인'이라는 뜻의 abstract와 다른, 신문 기사 투의 공식 표현.

entries.sense_en: to search for something by moving many things around

synonyms.nuance: General; can be careful and organized.
Search violently and leave a mess, usually to steal.
Search a pile or a deep container.

entries.sense_en: to state something under oath in court

synonyms.nuance: The usual word for giving evidence in court.
Promise something is true, in or out of court.
Say formally, not necessarily under oath.

entries.modern: "deposed to having heard" → "testified that she had heard"

entries.sense_en: to become known or come out as a fact

synonyms.nuance: Slowly become clear or known.
Everyday way to say the result became known.
synonyms.example: It turned out he was lying.

synonyms.nuance: Just an event; transpire is used loosely for this, which some dislike.

entries.sense_en: to join metal parts with melted metal

synonyms.nuance: Melts the parts themselves together; stronger and hotter.
Join by melting together, often figurative.
Uses a metal like brass; hotter than soldering.

entries.sense_en: quickly and without a full trial or formal process

synonyms.nuance: Right away; says nothing about lack of process.
Too quickly, often carelessly.
Informal: at once, in that place.

entries.sense_en: to search through something quickly in order to steal

synonyms.nuance: Wreck the place while searching.
Sudden attack to take things.
Steal in a disaster or riot.

entries.sense_en: to find out something for certain

synonyms.nuance: Everyday, informal.
Prove something with facts.
Formal; reach a fixed answer.

entries.sense_en: to turn to something for help when other things fail

synonyms.nuance: Turn to something less nice, as a last choice.
Everyday; ask or use for help.
Use a backup option.

entries.tip_ko: have recourse to / without recourse to 형태.

entries.sense_en: to give short flashes of light

synonyms.nuance: Steady soft light, longer than a glint.
Many bright flashes, showy.
A sudden strong burst of light.

entries.sense_en: one of the flat cut surfaces of a gem

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for any flat surface.
A flat surface of a solid shape.
Figurative: one part of an idea or situation.

entries.sense_en: suggesting evil or danger

synonyms.nuance: Warns that something bad will happen soon.
Threatening directly.
Plainly wicked; sinister only hints at it.

entries.sense_en: one who supplies something (here, figuratively, a thing that supplies people to the gallows and prison)

synonyms.nuance: Plain business word for one who supplies goods.
Gives something needed.
Sells goods, sometimes illegal ones.

entries.sense_en: friendly, warm and cheerful manner

synonyms.nuance: Everyday; feeling of kindness.
Easy to talk to, polite.
Simple and common.

entries.tip_ko: genius(천재)와 혼동하지 말 것: genial은 '상냥한, 쾌활한'.

entries.sense_en: a guess based on a few clues

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; needs no clues.
A feeling rather than reasoning.
Formal guess with incomplete evidence.

entries.tip_ko: 명사와 동사가 같은 형태이며 강세는 뒤(sur-MIZE).

entries.sense_en: looking embarrassed or ashamed

synonyms.nuance: Mild embarrassment after a small mistake.
Stronger, deep guilt.
General awkwardness in front of others.

entries.sense_en: showing off importance in a serious, overblown way

synonyms.nuance: Thinking oneself better than others; less comic.
Acting as if one matters greatly.
Pretending to be grander than one is.

entries.sense_en: with hands on hips and elbows pointing outward
entries.sense_ko: 두 손을 허리에 짚고 팔꿈치를 벌린

synonyms.nuance: Everyday description of the pose.
Only says something is crooked.

entries.sense_en: too sure of oneself (here used as a mocking name: "Mr. Cocksure")
entries.sense_ko: 지나치게 자신만만한 (여기서는 '잘난 척하는 양반'이라는 조롱조 호칭)

synonyms.nuance: Neutral: more confidence than facts justify.
Pleased with oneself in an annoying way.
Looks down on others.

entries.sense_en: annoyed and embarrassed at having failed or been wrong

synonyms.nuance: Awkward in front of others.
Mildly angry; less about shame.
Extremely embarrassed.

entries.sense_en: rude and bad-tempered

synonyms.nuance: Mildly bad-tempered, a bit comic.
Impolite; general.
Silent and sulking.

entries.sense_en: a loud confused noise from many voices

synonyms.nuance: Noisy excitement, may be a disturbance.
Louder, often angry.
Unpleasant loud noise.

entries.sense_en: to shrink back in fear or servility

synonyms.nuance: Crouch low in fear.
A quick small movement of pain or fear.
Behave humbly to win favor.

entries.sense_en: in a mild, calm, unbothered way that hides one's real feelings

synonyms.nuance: Simply without excitement.
Politely and without difficulty.
Gently, not sharply.

entries.sense_en: a false name used instead of one's real name

synonyms.nuance: A name an author uses, not necessarily to hide crime.
Friendly informal name.
Formal phrase for a made-up name.

entries.sense_en: a sudden piece of good luck, especially money

synonyms.nuance: Big prize in a game or lottery.
A large rich supply of something.
Lucky help at the right moment, not always money.

entries.sense_en: your secret plan has been discovered and you have been caught

synonyms.nuance: Same meaning, informal, mostly American.
Plain and direct.
Any ending; not just being caught.

entries.sense_en: without being punished or suffering bad results

synonyms.nuance: Informal: getting away without punishment.
Plain word for not punished.
Protection given by law or by the body.

entries.sense_en: a partner in a secret or criminal plan

synonyms.nuance: Common word for one who helps commit a crime.
Informal, sometimes joking.
Just a supporter; not necessarily criminal.

entries.sense_en: careful to act honestly and morally

synonyms.nuance: Truthful; scrupulous adds care about what is right.
Careful about doing one's duty well.
Acts by firm moral rules.

entries.sense_en: very dry, especially the mouth and lips from fear or thirst

synonyms.nuance: Plain word, any dryness.
Wanting a drink.
Dry land or climate.

entries.sense_en: to turn to a life of crime or immorality

synonyms.nuance: Wander from proper behavior.
Everyday: fail to live well, or make mistakes.
Lose control, behave badly.
synonyms.example: went off the rails at college

entries.modern: "went to the bad" → "went off the rails"

entries.sense_en: someone who has been in prison often

synonyms.nuance: The American spelling of the same word.
Someone currently serving a sentence.
Informal for a former prisoner.

entries.tip_ko: gaol은 영국식 옛 표기로 jail과 같은 발음이다.
